description:
Adapt FoundationDB's consumer-driven pop/trim model to Bedrock's log→Demux→ShardServer→object-storage architecture. This ticket states SUCCESS CRITERIA only; design doc to follow before implementation.

## Context (code as of today)

Each Shale log owns a Demux; ShardServers flush chunks to object storage and report {:durable, shard_id, v}; Demux sends min across active shards to the log as {:min_durable_version, v}; Shale trims closed segments with last_version <= min. Materializers still catch up from the WAL via Log.pull (the subscriber: {id, durable_version} option exists but Shale ignores it); ShardServer.pull/chunk catch-up exists but has no callers. Log recovery (recover_from) rewrites segments WITHOUT routing through Demux, and Demux state is neither reset nor replayed across recovery.

## Success criteria

### Correctness (floor never advances past data the WAL is the last copy of)
1. A shard's durability watermark only ever covers versions whose chunks are CONFIRMED in object storage. Specifically, shard activation must not claim the activating transaction's version as durable (today Durability.activate_shard uses last_seen_version while the slice is only buffered — a crash after trim loses the slice).
2. After recover_from, every version in the replayed range (recovery durable_version, last_version] either re-enters the Demux→chunk pipeline and gets confirmed, or the trim floor stays pinned at the recovery durable_version. No trim may free a segment whose data never reached object storage.
3. Stale Demux/ShardServer state (buffers, durability entries, in-flight flushes) from before a recover_from cannot flush discarded versions or advance the new floor. Versions above the recovery cut that were already flushed as chunks must be invisible to consumers (clamped or cleaned).
4. Trim only runs in mode == :running; the floor is clamped to last_version; watermark remains monotonic; segments straddling the floor are retained; the active segment is never trimmed. (Subsumes bedrock-8p4.)

### Completeness (every WAL consumer is accounted for)
5. Every consumer whose only catch-up path is the WAL contributes its floor to the trim min. Today that includes materializers: either (a) materializers catch up from snapshots + ShardServer chunks so the WAL floor is object-storage-only, or (b) materializer durable versions (the existing subscriber tuple on Log.pull) join the min until (a) lands. One of the two must hold at every commit of this work — no window where a materializer restart can land below the floor with no recovery path.
6. A pull/peek below the floor returns the floor as data (e.g. {:error, {:version_too_old, floor_version}}), not an opaque error, and materializers react by re-bootstrapping from object storage (snapshot + chunks) rather than circuit-breaking forever.

### Liveness (nothing pins the tail forever)
7. An idle shard (empty buffer, no new slices) does not pin the floor: with nothing unflushed, its contribution advances with the log's last seen version. (Today an idle shard freezes the min at its last flush.)
8. A shard whose flush permanently fails (PersistenceWorker drops after max_retries) fails fast (crash → recovery) instead of silently wedging flush_in_progress and freezing the floor.
9. A removed/reassigned shard is deactivated from durability tracking (Durability.deactivate_shard is wired up) so dead shards cannot pin the WAL indefinitely.
10. Under a lagging consumer, WAL growth is bounded by an explicit policy (hard limit with backpressure or documented unbounded-with-alerting) — not an accident.

### Signalling discipline (FDB lessons)
11. Watermark signals are idempotent, latest-wins, and coalesced; losing one is harmless because a higher one follows.
12. The floor need not be persisted by the log; on restart it regresses conservatively (segments on disk define oldest_version) and is re-derived from fresh confirmations.

### Observability
13. Telemetry identifies WHICH shard/consumer currently pins the floor (FDB's MinPoppedTag equivalent), the floor's version lag behind last_version, and bytes of WAL retained beyond the floor.
14. Trim events (segments recycled, floor advanced/rejected) are traced.

### Validation
15. Tests cover: crash-after-trim-before-flush (criterion 1), recovery-then-trim of the replayed range (2), stale-flush-after-recovery (3), materializer restart below the floor (6), idle-shard floor advancement (7), and dropped-flush fail-fast (8).

## DESIGN (approved 2026-08-15)

Core mechanism: versions ARE the clock. Demux computes fixed version-time buckets
(bucket = div(version_int, W_chunk), default W_chunk = 5_000_000 us) and on every bucket
crossing (heartbeats included; every log sees every version) broadcasts {:flush, cut_version}
(cut = last version of the closed bucket) to ALL its ShardServers. ShardServers are dumb:
flush everything <= cut as one chunk (put_if_not_exists; :already_exists = confirmation), or
confirm immediately if empty (idle shards never pin). A shard reports a FLOOR CONTRIBUTION
("everything I ever saw <= cut is safe"), = cut_version, not "max flushed". Wall-clock
(System.os_time) and version-gap flush heuristics are deleted.

Chunk naming (load-bearing): the file is named for the LAST COMMIT IT CONTAINS
(existing c/{shard}/{inverted-base36(max_contained)}). Object stores answer next-key-after
cheaply, so a reader seeking v does one list(start_after: key(v)). Cut is the flush TRIGGER,
never the file name; a name is a promise "nothing in me is newer than my name". Deterministic
cuts => deterministic content => deterministic names across replicas/replays.

Activation: a new shard's initial contribution = last completed cut (never a buffered version).
Shardless Demux contributes its last completed cut so heartbeat-only logs still trim.

Fail-fast: PersistenceWorker drop-after-max-retries notifies its owner; ShardServer crashes;
link chain (ShardServer -> Demux -> log) converts a permanently failing flush into recovery.

Recovery: recover_from tears down and restarts Demux (stale buffers/in-flight flushes die;
stale incarnation signals ignored via pid-tagged messages). BEFORE any replay flushes, a chunk
CLEANUP PASS deletes every chunk named above the recovery durable version -- by the naming
promise those are the only chunks that can contain discarded versions, and everything
committed above the floor is still in surviving WALs and will be re-produced identically by
replay (commits resume only after recovery completes, so no races). Cleanup runs once,
director-orchestrated in the log replay phase, before recover_from calls go out. Replay routes
through Demux; the floor starts pinned at the recovery durable version and advances only via
fresh confirmations. Trim: only in mode :running, clamped to last_version, monotonic,
straddling segments retained, active segment never trimmed (subsumes bedrock-8p4).

Consumers: Shale tracks the subscriber: {id, durable_version} tuple already sent on every
Log.pull and includes the min subscriber floor in the trim min, with a version-time TTL.
Aging out is safe because the floor is DATA: pull below floor returns
{:error, {:version_too_old, floor_version}} and olivine re-bootstraps from object storage
(snapshot + ShardServer chunks) instead of circuit-breaking forever. End state (with #115):
materializers leave the trim min entirely.

Growth policy: telemetry alarm when last_version - floor > lag limit (default 8 x W_chunk);
optional (config, default off) push rejection {:error, :wal_backpressure}. Default posture:
documented unbounded-with-alerting.

Telemetry: pinning shard/subscriber (MinPoppedTag equivalent), floor lag us, WAL bytes
retained beyond floor, trim/floor-advance trace events.

Phases (independently landable): P1 trim guards; P2 cut engine; P3 fail-fast; P4 recovery
(fresh Demux + cleanup + replay-through-Demux); P5 consumer floors + olivine re-bootstrap;
P6 telemetry + backpressure.

Non-goals: cross-epoch routing stability; persisted floor (regress conservatively on restart);
reader lease registry (MVCC-window side of the epic); per-shard quorum coverage (separate
ticket). Snapshot keys (s/{shard}/...) above the recovery cut are NOT cleaned by this work --
materializer-side concern, noted for the epic.
title: WAL tail trimming: consumer-driven floor signalling (FDB pop model adapted to Demux/object storage)
